items.title: Kidd Jordan interviewed by Monk Rowe, Rome, New York, August 24, 2006
items.q: when I’m with William [Parker] and I’m it I’m going to play off of William and he was going to lay something down for me to play off of so I could play.

ctx.x: Well I’m fascinated by, before the camera was rolling you were talking about the session a little bit and you showed up with sort of one thing in mind and the other two-thirds of your trio had something else in mind.

That’s right. Well I was thinking it was going to be like one of the sessions I usually do, we start playing in one of them knock-out drag-out sessions. And we’d get in there and play awful but we’d know, and when I’m with William [Parker] and I’m it I’m going to play off of William and he was going to lay something down for me to play off of so I could play. When it’s free we call it improvised. Some people call it free but it’s not as

free as you think it is. Because William will always lay down some keys, some things, some sounds and then pull it out from under me, and then I’ve got to go with him and then I get settled again and I have to somewhere else. So I mean it’s real improvised. But when I got in there and they started tinkling on the bells and hitting the gongs and the African instruments I said hey man, so and so and so. Now the first part of that was just a warm-up for me to try the mouthpiece. And they put that on there and named…
